page: Vultr vcg-a40-4c-20g-8vram is a fractional GPU instance within the Cloud GPU family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 2 physical Intel x86_64 cores running at 2.0 GHz, with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 20.0 GB of system memory, providing 5.0 GB per core. For acceleration, it bundles a fractional NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU with a 0.1667 allocation, providing 8 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage consists of a 360 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate highly specialized capabilities. The instance achieves top-tier results in LLM inference, processing 9881.81 tokens per second for small 135M model prompts and 3161.22 tokens per second for medium 7B model prompts. Text generation speeds are also strong, reaching 465.27 tokens per second on the small model and 107.91 tokens per second on the medium model. However, general compute and database performance show limitations. Passmark database operations and CPU encryption tests are rated as weak, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is poor. Standard CPU and memory benchmarks, such as stress-ng and Passmark CPU scores, fall into the average range.

This instance offers a cost-efficient entry point for GPU-accelerated workloads by utilizing a fractional GPU slice rather than a full dedicated card. This resource density makes it highly suitable for low-to-medium scale LLM inference, light machine learning model execution, and development environments. However, the tradeoff lies in its modest CPU performance and weaker database and web serving throughput. It is best suited for AI inference, lightweight data science tasks, and GPU-assisted development, rather than high-throughput web serving or heavy database operations.
